scope: P2PAudioSink is the sole ordinary one-to-one P2P remote audio owner and remains mounted across main-chat navigation. Remote video presentation is muted so its shared stream cannot produce duplicate or uncontrolled audio.

Remote audio tracks feed a WebAudio gain and MediaStreamDestination, then one routed audio element. The graph never also connects to AudioContext.destination. Master times peer-personal volume preserves zero and supports up to 200 percent; local mute, local deafen and server deafen silence remote playback without changing microphone publication or mute state.

Selected output is applied before playback. Only a missing selected device (NotFoundError) permits system-default fallback, which is disclosed in UI. Unsupported custom routing, permission denial, context/playback failure and ten-second hung operations fail explicitly with a retry action. No success is inferred merely from assigning a stream.

Output/call/stream/connection transitions and direct account/auth-generation subscriptions stop obsolete playback. Abort, pause, mute, srcObject detach and graph cleanup prevent late sink/play promises from reviving obsolete audio. Owned destination tracks are stopped; borrowed remote microphone/video tracks are not.

A WeakMap binds a stream to its first adopted account, auth generation, call, peer and connection. A retained previously adopted stream cannot be reassigned to another login or replacement call. This supplements current-store checks; it is not independent proof of signaling/authentication provenance before first adoption.

New remote audio tracks are mixed through the same controlled gain; removed/ended tracks detach. Device identifiers remain device-local through existing preference behavior. No server publication, microphone pipeline, group call capture or undeafen semantics changed.

Late old sink success/failure cannot replace a newer selected output; late play remains paused after cancellation
Dynamic remote tracks and cleanup without stopping borrowed microphone/video tracks
Master and personal zero, local mute, local/server deafen without transmission mutation
Retained adopted stream rejected after relogin, switching to other participant or component remount
Explicit failure/retry and stale readiness cannot clear replacement failure
Actual remote video DOM is muted while the dedicated audio owner reports fallback
Existing shared microphone/LiveKit/P2P capture and routing regression tests
